_comment: Fixtures for scripts/test_buildium_writes.py. Copy to a file you do NOT
commit (it names real records) and adjust if you are testing a different
account.
These are NAMES, not ids, on purpose: the prompts are natural language and
the agent resolves them the way a user would. That means the run also
tests entity resolution -- and if a name is ambiguous the agent should ASK
rather than guess, which is itself worth seeing (gotcha 41).
THE VALUES BELOW ARE REAL and verified against Blue Ridge Properties
(Buildium account 695763, company 5ca1ab1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000002)
on 2026-08-31, scoped to that company (gotcha 47):
property  200 E Colfax Ave  buildium_id 37953, Denver CO. ONE unit, ONE
active lease (115940, to 2027-03-18), ONE
open task (39467, New), ONE open work order
(11316, New). The smallest surface left in
the account, so 'the oldest open task' and
'the most recent open work order' each
resolve to exactly one record with nothing
to mis-join. The mirror prefixes it with a
state code and an em dash ('CO - 200 E
Colfax Ave' with a real em dash); the bare
street name is used here because the harness
is ASCII-only and that em dash is the exact
character that broke the script once.
unit      Unit 1            the unit_number really is the bare '1'.
vendor    Volt & Vine       one of Blue Ridge's three vendors. Vendors
are account-level, so this is unchanged.
tenant    Aaron Tillman     the CURRENT tenant (229933). Verified from
the ACTIVE lease, not any lease (gotcha 51).
!! A FORMER tenant (230131) also sits at this address -- a past lease
(116102) that ended 2026-03-13 and carries a real MoveOutData row. The
move-out confirm gate MUST name Tillman. If it names the former tenant,
that is a real finding (gotcha 51), not a fixture problem: decline it.
!! WHY THIS MOVED OFF 500 Woodlane St (37951), which this file named until
2026-08-31. That property was nominated as the permanent test record and
was the right choice for the first run only. After six dogfood passes it
held two work orders, an extra task, notes from four runs, and a lease
shortened to 2026-08-30 by the failed move-out (gotcha 70). The 2026-08-31
dry pass then measured its own residue: four of eleven tools never reached
a gate because the agent was correctly reasoning about records earlier
runs had created ('two open work orders at 500 Woodlane St'), and two more
hit the deadline re-verifying that state. A fixture property has to be
either disposable or restored between runs; 'smallest surface in the
account' is a property of the FIRST run only.
So: expect to move this again. When the reversible tier stops gating
cleanly, that is the residue signal, not a regression -- pick the next
single-unit property with one active lease, one open task and one open
work order, and record the previous one here.
!! 500 Woodlane St still needs a human in the Buildium UI: restore lease
115938 (Doyle Prather) to LeaseToDate 2026-09-14, and clear the extra work
order / task / notes. Nothing in this harness can do it -- lease dates are
not on any write tool's surface.
